title: Wedge-shaped pale kidney lesion + palpitations: renal infarction (cardioembolic)
vignette: A 54-year-old man comes to the hospital due to acute-onset right flank pain associated with nausea. Five years ago, the patient had nephrolithiasis; the renal calculi passed spontaneously with intravenous fluids. Review of systems is positive for occasional palpitations. Other medical problems include hypertension, obesity, and obstructive sleep apnea. Temperature is 38 C (100.4 F), blood pressure is 170/98 mm Hg, pulse is 90/min, and respirations are 18/min. Cardiopulmonary examination shows no abnormalities. Right flank tenderness is present. Urinalysis demonstrates 2+ red blood cells and no white blood cells or protein. A representative kidney specimen is shown below: the specimen shows a sharply demarcated pale wedge-shaped area with surrounding hyperemia. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

clues.note: Intermittent palpitations (with obesity/sleep apnea) suggest atrial fibrillation - a source of cardioembolism to the renal artery.
Acute hypertension can result from renin release by ischemic (infarcted) renal tissue.

clues.text: 2+ red blood cells and no white blood cells or protein
clues.note: Hematuria WITHOUT pyuria or proteinuria fits infarction/vascular injury rather than infection (pyelonephritis) or glomerular disease.

clues.text: sharply demarcated pale wedge-shaped area with surrounding hyperemia
clues.note: A sharply demarcated, pale, WEDGE-SHAPED area with hyperemic rim is the classic gross appearance of a RENAL INFARCT (coagulative necrosis in a vascular territory).

whatMatters: Acute flank pain + hematuria (no pyuria/proteinuria) + palpitations (atrial fibrillation) + a sharply demarcated, pale, WEDGE-SHAPED lesion with hyperemic margin = RENAL INFARCTION, most often from CARDIOEMBOLIC disease (AF). Answer D.
strategy: Read the gross image (pale wedge-shaped infarct) with the clinical clues (embolic source = AF/palpitations; hematuria without infection/protein). Renal infarcts are wedge-shaped because they follow the vascular territory of an occluded end-artery. Reject nephrolithiasis (obstruction/hydronephrosis, no infarct), pyelonephritis (pyuria/WBC casts, focal abscesses), renal cell carcinoma (solid yellow mass with hemorrhage, not a pale wedge), and papillary necrosis (sloughed papillae from analgesics/diabetes/sickle cell, not a cortical wedge).

eliminations.label: Nephrolithiasis - obstruction, not infarct
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: renal calculi causing colicky flank pain and hematuria. ❌ WHY IT FAILS: stones cause obstruction/hydronephrosis (dilated calyces), not a pale wedge-shaped parenchymal infarct. ✅ Correct if: stone with hydronephrosis on imaging.

eliminations.label: Pyelonephritis - pyuria expected
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: bacterial kidney infection with flank pain, fever, and nausea. ❌ WHY IT FAILS: pyelonephritis shows PYURIA (WBCs/WBC casts) and often dysuria; this urinalysis has RBCs but NO WBCs, and the gross lesion is an infarct, not focal abscesses. ✅ Correct if: pyuria/WBC casts with dysuria.

eliminations.label: Renal cell carcinoma - solid yellow mass
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: a renal parenchymal malignancy that can cause flank pain and hematuria. ❌ WHY IT FAILS: RCC is a solid, well-circumscribed YELLOW mass with hemorrhage/necrosis, not a pale, sharply demarcated wedge-shaped infarct. ✅ Correct if: a golden-tan renal mass (clear cell RCC).

eliminations.label: Papillary necrosis - sloughed papillae
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: ischemic necrosis of the renal PAPILLAE (analgesic overuse, diabetes, sickle cell, obstruction). ❌ WHY IT FAILS: it shows necrotic, sloughing papillae with cortical atrophy at the medulla, not a cortical wedge-shaped infarct. ✅ Correct if: sloughed papillae/gross hematuria with predisposing condition.

reasoning: Acute flank pain with hematuria but no pyuria/proteinuria points to a vascular event
Occasional palpitations suggest atrial fibrillation (an embolic source)
The gross specimen shows a sharply demarcated, pale, wedge-shaped infarct with hyperemic rim
mechanism: RENAL INFARCTION results from acute occlusion of a renal artery or its branches, most commonly by CARDIOEMBOLIC disease - ATRIAL FIBRILLATION (suggested here by palpitations, obesity, and sleep apnea) is the greatest risk factor, though mural thrombus after MI, valvular vegetations, direct arterial injury (dissection, vasculitis), and hypercoagulable states also cause it. The kidney is prone to embolic infarction because of its high perfusion and limited collateral circulation. Because renal arteries are functional END-ARTERIES, occlusion produces COAGULATIVE NECROSIS in the vascular territory, giving a sharply demarcated, PALE (yellow-white), WEDGE-SHAPED infarct with a HYPEREMIC border on gross pathology. Typical features are acute FLANK PAIN, nausea/vomiting, low-grade fever, HEMATURIA (with a normal or mildly abnormal urinalysis - RBCs but not pyuria/proteinuria), elevated LDH, and HYPERTENSION from renin release by ischemic tissue. The distractors are obstructive (nephrolithiasis), infectious (pyelonephritis - pyuria), neoplastic (RCC - solid yellow mass), or papillary (papillary necrosis) processes that don't produce a cortical wedge infarct.

difficulty.label: 🧠 Knowledge
difficulty.text: First Aid Renal > renal infarction: cardioembolic (atrial fibrillation #1); end-artery -> wedge-shaped pale coagulative infarct with hyperemic rim; flank pain, hematuria without pyuria, elevated LDH, hypertension (renin).

difficulty.label: 📖 Comprehension
difficulty.text: Wedge-shaped pale infarct + AF/palpitations + hematuria without infection = renal infarction.

difficulty.label: 🔤 Vocab
difficulty.text: Unsure on renal infarction, coagulative necrosis, end-artery, cardioembolism, or wedge-shaped infarct? Tell me which.

difficulty.label: 🨤 Distractor
difficulty.text: Stones = obstruction; pyelonephritis = pyuria; RCC = solid yellow mass; papillary necrosis = sloughed papillae.

difficulty.label: 🖼️ Imaging / diagram
difficulty.text: Gross kidney specimen (stem): sharply demarcated pale WEDGE-shaped area with a hyperemic rim = renal infarct (coagulative necrosis in a vascular territory).

difficulty.label: 🗒️ Other
difficulty.text: Bank: renal infarction = cardioembolic (AF); wedge-shaped pale infarct; hematuria without pyuria; high LDH.

keywords.back: Sharply demarcated, pale, wedge-shaped, hyperemic rim
RCC = solid yellow mass; infarct = pale wedge

firstAid.detail: Renal > stones, pyelonephritis, RCC, papillary necrosis.
CV > embolic source for renal/systemic infarcts.

memoryHook: A pale pie-slice (wedge) carved into the kidney with a red rim = an infarct; the culprit clot usually flew in from a fibrillating atrium.
